headline: US Consumer Confidence Rises to 91.7 in October, Beating Expectations
summary: US consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in the previous month. The reading significantly exceeded economists' forecasts of 81 as households reported an improved economic outlook.
why: Consumer spending accounts for more than two-thirds of US economic activity, making confidence surveys a key leading indicator of retail sales and overall macroeconomic growth.
why_moved: Stronger-than-expected consumer sentiment data reassures investors regarding consumer spending momentum, boosting domestic economic growth prospects.
